rows.note: 042 took the dimple tolerance 9.318-16.057 mm (width 0.357 m) from the 015b map as the shape that delivers gamma 0.564. My elastic FE of the 028b section (the CHECK-029 model) gives 0.511 and 0.469 there. It reaches 0.564 only at a dimple of 5.82 mm or less. Keeping the core within its typical shear strength at operating needs 2.38 mm or less (1.80 mm at the minimum strength). Keeping the outer face below 345 MPa needs 1.27 mm or less. The article seeds several amplitudes so that the test settles which is right.
rows.proposed_fix: Seed 2, 6 and 16 mm dimples (one article each) and report gamma against amplitude, not one number.

rows.note: On the 028b section, the core reaches CR III W typical shear (35 psi) at 24.9 kPa (16 mm dimple) and at 37.8 kPa (9.3 mm), long before the elastic limit. A test article at those amplitudes will most likely fail by core shear on the dimple flank (r about 280-430 mm) before global collapse. Its measured pressure is then a core-strength capacity, and the outcome table records the mode with the value.

The p_cl-matched 5052-O face (3.103 mm on a 20.929 mm core, h held) reproduces beryllium's elastic gamma within +2.8% and its core-shear onset within +2.6%. Its outer face reaches yield at 0.88 of beryllium's pressure; the operating-stress ratio matches to 0.99. Not matched: biaxial membrane stiffness (+31%, from nu 0.33 against 0.0752), the wrinkle margin (x4.0, so wrinkling is suppressed), beryllium's low-ductility fracture, and the line's Be compression premise (the match uses the 345 MPa tensile proxy). A Be confirmation article is needed before any qualification claim.
rows.proposed_fix: Re-match the stand-in thickness after 038 T1 measures SR-200 compression.

rows.note: The homogenized CR III core with E_in 0.01 MPa loses ellipticity at about 0.088 MPa shear, and these paths pass that at 7-11 kPa. So an FE on a mesh fine enough to resolve the dimple flank cannot predict the core's response there. The test, not the FE, has to supply it. The pre-test FE needs a sourced in-plane core law or a cell model.

In my elastic FE, the clamped edge of the 5 m cap yields the inner face and crushes the core at about 60 kPa. That is edge bending and not part of the sphere's behaviour. The dimple region itself matches the sphere: the limit is within +1.4%, core-shear onset within -0.4%, and outer-face yield within +0.5%.
rows.proposed_fix: Design a reinforced edge (face doublers, potted core ring) and check it before the build.

rows.note: The R30 section at 1/3 on R 10 m (0.822 / 34.20 mm) keeps R/h, Vc, dimple/t_eq and stresses, but the 9.5 mm cell is unscaled. That gives 4.5 cells per wrinkle wavelength against 13.6 at full R30, and cell/h of 0.27 against 0.09. Its cap needs a base radius of 3 m: 2.5 m gives -2.2% and 3 m gives +1.2%.

No commercial external-pressure chamber found takes a 5-6 m article; the largest found are 2.3 m ID (FET), 1.6 m (Matrix) and Tyne's TPT5 (4.5 m long). The rig is therefore evacuation under the cap plus a water head above it. The hydrostatic gradient over the 0.32-0.46 m rise is 3.1-4.5 kPa (about 3% at 120 kPa), and the pole sees the lowest pressure. Collapse dynamics under water and tank safety are open.

Under 90/95 normal tolerance statistics, three articles at 5% scatter need a mean of 0.815 to bound 0.564, and at 10% scatter it is impossible. Ten articles at 10% need 0.738. So a result counts under a validated-analysis rule: at least three articles per configuration, measured as-built shape, identified failure mode, and an elastic-plastic FE that predicts each within 10%. Precedent: NASA SBKF used 8 subscale and 2 full-scale cylinders.

Reis 2017's plateau knockdown (0.447 at lambda 1) and its single-parameter scaling are for homogeneous elastic hemispheres. Their transfer to Vc near 1 sandwiches, with t_eq = sqrt(3) h, is unproven.
My FE is elastic (StVK) and axisymmetric. Its limits are elastic limits; with face yield and core failure the real capacity at these dimples is lower. Nonaxisymmetric modes are not modelled.
